title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 158 (Obligation to indicate Director Identification Number)

content.overview: Section 158 requires every person or company, while furnishing any return, information or particulars as are required to be furnished under the Act, to mention the Director Identification Number in such return, information or particulars in case such return, information or particulars relate to the director or contain any reference of any director.
content.glance: DIN must be quoted in every return, information or particular under the Act that relates to or refers to a director.
content.study: Every person or company, while furnishing any return, information or particulars as are required to be furnished under this Act, shall mention the Director Identification Number in such return, information or particulars in case such return, information or particulars relate to the director or contain any reference of any director. Quoting a wrong number is a contravention attracting the penalty under section 159. Current-law framing: identify the filing; check whether it relates to or refers to a director; confirm DIN is correctly quoted.

sections.heading: Who Must Quote
sections.body: Every person or company furnishing a return, information or particulars under the Act.

sections.heading: When
sections.body: Where the return, information or particulars relate to the director or contain any reference to any director.

sections.heading: What
sections.body: The Director Identification Number of the director concerned must be mentioned.

sections.heading: Consequence of Wrong Quote
sections.body: Quoting a wrong DIN is a contravention dealt with under section 159.

provisions.title: Obligation to indicate Director Identification Number

examples.title: Annual return
examples.body: A company’s annual return lists directors. Under s. 158 each director’s DIN must be quoted in the return.

examples.title: Wrong DIN
examples.body: A filing quotes an incorrect DIN for a director. Section 158 is breached and s. 159 penalty is engaged.

hypotheticals.question: Must DIN be quoted in a document that does not relate to or refer to any director?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 158 applies only where the return, information or particulars relate to the director or contain a reference to any director.

distinctions.title: Obligation to indicate DIN (s. 158) vs company to inform DIN to ROC (s. 157)
distinctions.left: Duty to quote DIN in any relevant filing or particular
distinctions.right: Company’s duty to furnish DINs to the Registrar after intimation

misconceptions.trap: DIN need only be quoted once at appointment and never again.
misconceptions.correction: Section 158 requires the DIN whenever a return, information or particular under the Act relates to or refers to the director.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 158 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify the filing. II. Check if it relates to or refers to a director. III. Confirm DIN quoted correctly. IV. Link to s. 159 if wrong. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Filing facts; DIN quote status; precise relief.

examTips: Quote DIN whenever the filing relates to or refers to a director.
